inputs.share_count_basis: 73.611m shares outstanding net of treasury at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin); FY2026 annual report note states diluted EPS is not presented because there are no potential shares. Held flat: no SBC, buybacks de minimis (JPY 2m FY2026).
inputs.net_debt_note: Q1 FY2027 balance sheet (30 Jun 2026): short-term borrowings 11,560 + current portion of long-term borrowings 10,295 + long-term borrowings 64,070 = 85,925; cash and deposits 75,995. Lease liabilities (~JPY 2.2bn) excluded, consistent with the lease treatment. FY2026 year-end (31 Mar 2026) was 86,123 debt / 77,763 cash = 8,360 net debt; debt roughly doubled in FY2026 from 42,212.
inputs.sbc_source: JGAAP filer; no share-based payment line in the FY2026 consolidated statements (SBC fields NULL in the metrics table). Treated as zero, kept as an explicit 0% row. House and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income JPY 180m is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt (JPY 9.9bn), so there is no cash pile being double-counted. Dividend income on cross-shareholdings sits below operating profit and is therefore already outside the EBITDA-built flows; the matching asset (investment securities) is added in the equity bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: Purchase of treasury shares JPY 2m in FY2026 (odd-lot repurchases only). No buyback programme; the flat share count is a modelling convention the company has not had to pay for, which is fine here because there is no SBC to offset.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% built in JPY: 10y JGB ~1.7%, Japan ERP 6.5%, beta 1.25 for a cyclical capital-goods maker with two loss years in the sample (FY2015-16) -> cost of equity ~9.8%; ~17% debt weight (JPY 86bn borrowings vs JPY 433bn market cap) at ~1.0% after-tax -> ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality, order lumpiness and the balance-sheet strain are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: JGAAP: operating leases are expensed inside operating profit (already in EBITDA); finance-lease liabilities of ~JPY 2.2bn (608 current + 1,623 non-current at 31 Mar 2026) are immaterial and excluded from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is already inside the EBITDA margin. One treatment: leases as operating cost.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests JPY 1,400m (31 Mar 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated. NCI dividends were JPY 2m in FY2026 so the leakage is negligible either way.
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax rate 30.5% flat: FY2026 income taxes paid JPY 8,247m against pre-tax profit of ~JPY 27bn (~30%), in line with Japan's ~30.6% statutory effective rate. No carryforward or one-off benefit in the latest year.
inputs.capex_note: JGP2028 (updated Jul 2026) budgets cumulative capital investment of JPY 111.5bn over FY2024-FY2028; FY2024-26 spent 9.9 + 15.1 + 23.7 = 48.7bn, leaving ~63bn for FY2027-28 (~31bn/yr, ~10% and ~9% of revenue). Hiroshima assembly/machining shops and Muroran forging capacity (rotor shafts +50%, nuclear forgings doubling) complete through FY2028; capex then normalises to 4.5% of revenue by year 6 against D&A rising to 4.0% as the new assets depreciate.
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer with work-in-process of JPY 123bn and contract liabilities of 57bn against payables of 25bn: growth consumes cash. JGP2028 shows a cumulative JPY 126bn working-capital increase over FY2024-28 (Subcontract Act payment-term shortening plus long-WIP defense and materials orders); FY2025-26 consumed ~75bn against ~22bn of revenue growth, partly the one-off payment-term step. wc_capture_pct is -35% of the YoY revenue change in all scenarios, which reproduces the plan's FY2027 net-debt path (owner FCF ~ -JPY 15bn in year 1 vs the plan's implied ~ -12bn) without perpetuating the one-off step.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (margins and capex still normalising at year 5), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as a cyclical non-US operating company (industrial machinery, defense forgings, nuclear/thermal power components) with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: JPY-built WACC, SBC-zero market (band collapses; band_position null), JGAAP leases expensed, NCI once in the bridge, investment securities added as the matching asset for the dividend income excluded from EBITDA. FY0 is FY2026 (FYE 31 Mar 2026) with FY2027 guidance (sales 310bn, OP 27bn, reaffirmed at Q1 Aug 2026) as year 1. The reported FY2026 FCF of -JPY 40.6bn is a capex-and-working-capital supercycle year, not steady state: the model does not normalise FY0 FCF by hand but lets the component build run the FY2027-28 investment peak explicitly (negative owner FCF in years 1-2) and recover to a mid-cycle margin of ~5% of revenue by year 6. Terminal cap 15x (cyclical with two loss years in the sample), 12x in the bear. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF.

equity_bridge.note: JPY 23,401m at 30 Jun 2026 (Q1 FY2027 balance sheet), haircut 25% for tax on embedded gains and marketability. Matching asset for the dividend income that sits below operating profit and is therefore outside the EBITDA-built flows. The company is monetising these (JPY 6.7bn proceeds FY2026, JPY 2.1bn gain Q1 FY2027; JGP2028 plans ~JPY 7bn more).
31 Mar 2026 balance sheet; charged once here, flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5-yr CAGR (22.8%) diverges >30% from the equity CAGR (8.6%) and revenue CAGR (6.8%): EPS is rebounding off a depressed FY2021 base (JPY 93.76), not compounding at that rate. The 10-year revenue CAGR FY2016-FY2026 is only ~2.1%; the business is cyclical, not a steady grower.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: owner FCF (= reported FCF, SBC zero, interest income not stripped) was JPY 6,436m in FY2021, 13,520m in FY2022, -7,093m in FY2023, 11,843m in FY2024, -19,677m in FY2025 and -40,586m in FY2026. Negative endpoints make a CAGR meaningless; the series is dominated by the FY2025-26 working-capital and capex build. Mid-cycle owner FCF over FY2018-FY2024 averaged ~JPY 6.4bn (2.9% of revenue) on capex of 3-5% of revenue.

base.growth_note: Year 1 = FY2027 guidance (JPY 310bn, +12.8%, reaffirmed Aug 2026). Year 2 +12% takes FY2028 to ~JPY 347bn, about 87% of the JGP2028 target of 400bn, because the company missed its prior-plan FY2026 sales (320bn planned, 275bn delivered), defense orders fell 28% in FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 sales were -14% YoY. Fades to 2.5% by year 9.
base.margin_note: FY2027 guided OP 27bn + D&A ~10bn = 11.9% EBITDA margin (down from 12.5% in FY2026 on mix and start-up costs). Matures to 13.5%, just below the plan's FY2028 13.75% (EBITDA 55bn / 400bn), as higher-margin defense, nuclear forgings and aftermarket grow and the new capacity is absorbed.

bull.growth_note: Hits the raised JGP2028 plan: FY2028 revenue ~JPY 366bn by year 2 and 400bn+ by year 3 (plan 400bn FY2028 is reached a year late), with the FY2033 vision of 500bn approached by year 7-8. Margin reaches 14.5%, above the plan's 13.75%, on defense and nuclear mix.

bear.growth_note: FY2027 misses guidance (+5% after the -14% Q1), the defense order air-pocket and a molding-machine downturn roll through FY2028-29 (0%, -6%), then a slow recovery. The FY2027-28 capex is already committed so it is spent anyway; EBITDA margin troughs at 9% (the FY2021-23 range) and settles at 10.5%. Working-capital release in the down years cushions cash.

scenario_narratives.base: JSW delivers FY2027 guidance (sales JPY 310bn, OP 27bn) and grows toward but not to the raised JGP2028 targets, reaching ~JPY 347bn in FY2028 and ~JPY 400bn around FY2030. The Hiroshima and Muroran capacity programmes complete on schedule, with capex of ~JPY 31bn/yr in FY2027-28 and the working-capital build from the Subcontract Act and long-WIP defense/nuclear orders continuing at 35% of incremental revenue, so owner FCF is negative for two more years and net debt peaks near the plan's ~JPY 69bn before cash generation recovers. The EBITDA margin dips to 11.9% in FY2027 and matures at 13.5% as defense, nuclear forgings and aftermarket mix improve, giving a mid-cycle owner-FCF margin of ~5% of revenue by year 6. Terminal value is bound by the 15x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Both structural tailwinds land at once: Japan's defense build-up keeps artillery, armoured-vehicle and missile-canister orders at or above the FY2025 peak, and the European/US nuclear new-build cycle plus AI/data-centre-driven thermal investment fills the doubled Muroran forging capacity. Revenue reaches the JGP2028 JPY 400bn target a year late and approaches the FY2033 vision of 500bn by year 8; EBITDA margin reaches 14.5% on the richer mix and aftermarket growth. The same capex and working-capital burden applies in years 1-2, so the bull case still shows negative owner FCF initially; the difference is the scale of the business it converts into.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2026 defense order drop (-28%) and the Q1 FY2027 sales decline (-14%) prove to be the start of an order air-pocket rather than timing noise: FY2027 comes in at +5%, FY2028 flat and FY2029 -6% as the molding-machine business loses share to Haitian and European makers while EV battery-film and China capex stay weak. The FY2027-28 capex is already committed and is spent into a softer market, so the new capacity is under-absorbed and the EBITDA margin troughs at 9% (FY2021-23 levels) before settling at 10.5%. Net debt stays elevated longer and Japanese rate normalisation raises interest costs. No loss year is modelled, but the FY2015-16 losses are the reminder that project cost overruns in this business can go further than this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default: operating cash flow has been negative in three of the last four years, borrowings doubled in FY2026 to fund it, defense orders fell 28% and Q1 FY2027 sales fell 14%, and the sample contains two loss years (FY2015-16). Bull cut to 25% from 35%: the bull case needs defense, nuclear forgings and plastics machinery to all deliver simultaneously, and the company missed its own prior FY2026 sales plan by 14%. Base 50%: FY2027 guidance was reaffirmed in August and the medium-term order book (nuclear, defense) is visible.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value JSW as a cyclical capital-goods maker mid-way through a capex and working-capital supercycle: run the FY2027-28 investment peak explicitly in the flows rather than normalising the -JPY 40.6bn FY2026 FCF by hand, then capitalise a mid-cycle owner-FCF margin of ~5% of revenue at a capped 15x multiple. The stock trades at ~22x FY2027 guided EPS and ~13x EV/EBITDA, a multiple that already prices the JGP2028 plan; the DCF asks what the business is worth if the plan is delivered at ~85% and the cash finally arrives in FY2029 onwards.
key_risks_to_valuation: Working-capital capture: at -35% of incremental revenue the model reproduces the plan's FY2027 net-debt path; if the Subcontract Act step is fully behind and capture is nearer -20%, base value rises materially (every 5pp of capture is ~JPY 1.5-2bn/yr of FCF in the growth years).

Terminal cap at 15x FCF binds in the base and bull; a buyer paying the stock's current ~13x EV/EBITDA on a mature margin would value it higher. The cap is the cyclical-discipline rule and is the single largest driver of the gap to the market price.
Order lumpiness: defense orders of JPY 116bn in FY2025 vs 87bn in FY2026; one large MOD contract in either direction moves a year's revenue by 10%+.
Capex overrun or delay at Muroran/Hiroshima extends the negative-FCF window beyond FY2028.
Investment securities are added at 75% of book (JPY 17.6bn, ~JPY 238/share); the company is realising them, so the haircut is conservative but the asset is real.
